title: Cenotes, Jungles and Mountains: The Geography of the South
goal: Describe the cenotes of Yucatán, the Lacandon jungle and the cloud forests of Oaxaca with relative clauses.
grammar: relative clauses with que, donde and a preposition + el que

sections.title: Unit 3: The South: Indigenous Peoples and Biodiversity
body: This unit is about southern Mexico: Oaxaca, Chiapas and the Yucatán peninsula. You will read about the landscape, the Zapotec, Mixtec and Maya peoples, community government in Oaxaca, the Zapatista uprising of 1994 and the debate about the Maya Train.

The screens and instructions are in English; the texts and exercises are in Spanish. There is no new grammar here: each lesson uses a skill you already know to talk about the region, and teaches you the words you need for it.

items: I can describe a place or a thing with a relative clause (*que*, *donde*, *en el que*).
I can say what a cenote is and why the Maya held it sacred.
I can explain why the water of the Yucatán peninsula is easy to pollute.
